description: Creates a new Dreamlit workflow draft or updates an existing draft from an outcome-oriented natural-language prompt. Use after get_status; use get_workflow_and_preview_url first when editing an existing workflow, then describe the steps to change by what they do, not by step id. Each call continues the workflow's current chat; pass startNewChat to start fresh. Broadcasts that are scheduled, sent, or cancelled can't be edited; duplicate them in the Dreamlit web app instead. Existing Supabase Auth workflows can be edited except for the immutable trigger step; creating Supabase Auth workflows must happen through Supabase Auth email setup in the Dreamlit web app. Side effect: may create or modify a draft, but does not publish or install live triggers. Returns the workflow/draft result, action-required or handoff details when more input is needed, and relevant app URLs. Do not use for publishing, direct database changes, or low-level graph edits.

name.description: Name for a new workflow draft. Use when the user names the workflow; otherwise Dreamlit picks one. Only valid when creating; use rename_workflow to rename an existing workflow.

projectId.description: Target project id for creating a new workflow draft.

prompt.description: Outcome-oriented workflow authoring request. Describe the event or schedule, audience, recipient, message goal, data needed, timing, business rules, and unsubscribe intent. When editing, refer to existing steps by what they do (for example, the query that finds returning customers, or the email with subject "Welcome back"), never by step id. Let Dreamlit choose email styling unless the user gives specific style direction. For broadcasts, request a future send time instead of an immediate send.

startNewChat.description: Start a fresh Dreamlit chat for this request instead of continuing the workflow's current chat. The new chat still sees the current draft but not earlier turns. Use when switching to an unrelated change, after long turns with pasted SQL or HTML, or when Dreamlit keeps misreading the request. Ignored when creating a workflow.

userCurrentTimeIso.description: User's current time as an ISO timestamp with offset, useful for relative schedule requests.

userCurrentTimeZoneId.description: IANA timezone id for the user, useful for repeating workflows and scheduled broadcasts.

userEmailStepComments.description: Optional inline comments for revising email step content.

onCodeLineText.description: Nearby email editor text for anchoring the comment.

userHighlightedText.description: Specific text selected by the user.

workflowStepId.description: Workflow step id that the user commented on.

workflowId.description: Existing workflow id to continue editing. Use get_workflow_and_preview_url first when changing an existing workflow.

name: create_or_update_workflow

result.description: Dreamlit MCP result. success responses contain data and appUrls when relevant; auth_required, clarification_required, confirmation_required, handoff_required, and error responses explain the next action.

expectedEditableVersionId.description: Editable version id returned by prepare_publish, used as a safety check.

expectedPublishedVersionId.description: Published version id returned by prepare_publish, used as a safety check.

expectedUpdatedAtIso.description: Workflow updatedAt timestamp returned by prepare_publish, used as a safety check.

isSandboxed.description: Whether to publish in sandbox mode so notifications are held for inspection.

messageType.description: Optional message type filter when selecting a draft message to test.

rowData.description: Optional sample data for rendering draft message variables during the test. If omitted, Dreamlit uses the same default preview data as the web builder when available.

testRecipientEmail.description: Optional recipient for email tests. If omitted, Dreamlit sends to the authenticated user's email address.

testTargetId.description: Structured test target id from testableMessages. Do not show this id to users; ask them to choose by message label.

workflowId.description: Workflow id whose editable draft message should be tested.

blocker.description: Why Dreamlit stopped before finishing the draft. Changes counted in appliedActionCount are already saved.

code.description: step_needs_detail: answer `detail` in a follow-up create_or_update_workflow call with the same workflowId. step_not_editable: change a different step instead. step_not_built: retry once, then finish in the browser. request_unclear: describe the change in more detail and retry.

detail.description: The specific missing detail or blocking rule, in plain language.

billingUrl.description: quota_exceeded: page where a workspace admin can buy more AI credits.

helpUrl.description: Guide for fixing the problem in the message.

resetAt.description: quota_exceeded: when this month's AI usage resets (ISO 8601).

stepEdits.description: edit_workflow_steps: what happened to each edit when none could be applied.

code.description: step_not_found: get fresh step ids from get_workflow_and_preview_url. step_not_editable: triggers can't be edited here; use create_or_update_workflow. field_not_for_step_type: send only fields for that step's type. duplicate_step: combine edits to one step. invalid_value: fix the value as the message says. query_failed: fix the SQL. query_drops_used_fields: keep returning fields, or edit the steps that use them in the same call. related_edit_failed: a related edit in this call (a SQL edit above or below this step) failed; fix it and send both again. save_failed: try again.

fields.description: query_drops_used_fields: fields later steps still use that the new query no longer returns.

index.description: Position of the edit in the request.

unreadableTables.description: table_rows_hidden_by_rls: tables Dreamlit can see but not read rows from, each with fixSql that adds Dreamlit's read policy. Run fixSql, or ask the user to run it, in the Supabase SQL editor, then try again.
